# Introduction

This is my final project looking into UFC fight statistics including striking and takedowns and comparing the analysis we find related to these variables.

# Data Source

The UFC data used in this project was obtained from the ufc.stats package, developed by [mtoto](https://rdrr.io/github/mtoto/ufc.stats/f/README.md). The dataset includes updated statistics from official UFC fight records.





## Packages


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Same packages from the bike project
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(caret)
# Data Cleaning
library(stringr)
library(purrr)
# Different themes
library(ggthemes)
```
:::


## Data Set

I found a package that was conveniently already available on R that included up to date statistics. Below is the installation code I input in the console followed by the library used for this project.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
devtools::install_github("mtoto/ufc.stats")
data("ufc_stats")
```
:::

::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(ufc.stats)
```
:::

::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Update data
refresh_data()
data("ufc_stats")
```
:::

The data available has been cleaned for the most part, but looking at the last code output we see that the data is broken down into 'rounds'. I aggregated the data to be broken down into fights using multiple variables to group observations and also made the following modifications.

## Cleaning

::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Remove 'attendance' variable
ufc_cleaner <- ufc_stats %>%
  select(-attendance)
```
:::

Looking at the first few rows of ufc_stats we can see that all the values for 'attendance' are null. This isn't a variable I'm concerned about so I removed it from the data set entirely.

::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Create fight-end indicator
ufc_cleaner <- ufc_cleaner %>%
  mutate(fight_end = paste0("Round ", last_round, " - ", time))
```
:::

This variable will still show how many rounds each fight lasts followed by the time left in the round.

::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Create a unique opponent lookup table
opponent_lookup <- ufc_cleaner %>%
  select(id, fighter) %>%
  # Ensure unique fighters with fight 'id'
  distinct() %>%            
  group_by(id) %>%
  # Only keep fights with 2 fighters
  filter(n() == 2) %>%     
  # Reverse fighters for correct pairing
  mutate(opponent = rev(fighter)) %>% 
  ungroup()
```
:::

This table helps add an 'opponent' variable to each observation that I then joined with the clean ufc_cleaner table

::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Left join to add 'opponent_lookup' to 'ufc_cleaner'
ufc_cleaned <- ufc_cleaner %>%
  left_join(opponent_lookup, by = c("id", "fighter"))
```
:::


## Aggreate 

::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
ufc_agg <- ufc_cleaned %>%
  group_by(
    id, fighter, opponent, winner, result, event, fight_date, location, fight_end, scheduled_rounds
  ) %>%
  summarize(
    weight_classes = paste(unique(weight_class), collapse = ", "),
    knockdowns = sum(knockdowns, na.rm = TRUE),
    sig_strikes_landed = sum(significant_strikes_landed, na.rm = TRUE),
    sig_strikes_attempted = sum(significant_strikes_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    takedown_landed = sum(takedown_successful, na.rm = TRUE),
    takedown_attempted = sum(takedown_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    submission_attempt = sum(submission_attempt, na.rm = TRUE),
    head_landed = sum(head_landed, na.rm = TRUE),
    head_attempted = sum(head_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    body_landed = sum(body_landed, na.rm = TRUE),
    body_attempted = sum(body_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    leg_landed = sum(leg_landed, na.rm = TRUE),
    leg_attempted = sum(leg_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    clinch_landed = sum(clinch_landed, na.rm = TRUE),
    clinch_attempted = sum(clinch_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    ground_landed = sum(ground_landed, na.rm = TRUE),
    ground_attempted = sum(ground_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
:::

This code chunk is merging the raw data set I started with making it so that each observation includes information on a fight to fight basis versus by rounds. Below is an example of how I looked up a fighter to check ufc_agg along with the columns of the table that I'll be using for this project.

## Average Number of Signigicant Strikes

I wanted to see if Max Holloway's large total_significant_strike was attributed to him having a significantly larger number of fights while also looking at the average number of significant strikes a fight with other fighters.

```{.r .cell-code}
# Summarize total significant strikes and number of fights to create `avg_n_sstrikes`
most_sstrikes <- ufc_agg %>%
  group_by(fighter) %>%
  summarize(
    total_fights = n(),
    total_significant_strikes = sum(sig_strikes_landed)

  mutate(avg_n_sstrikes = round(total_significant_strikes / total_fights, 2)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_significant_strikes))
```

## fight_records_sstrikes

::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
# table with fight record of fighters while including more variables
fight_records_and_sstrikes <- ufc_agg %>%
  group_by(fighter) %>%
  summarize(
    total_fights = n(),
    wins = sum(winner == "W", na.rm = TRUE),
    losses = sum(winner == "L", na.rm = TRUE),
    total_significant_strikes = sum(sig_strikes_landed, na.rm = TRUE)
) %>%
  mutate(
    avg_n_sstrikes = round(total_significant_strikes / total_fights, 2),
    win_percentage = wins / total_fights) %>%
  # Arrange in descending order of `wins` & ascending order of `losses`
  arrange(-wins, +losses)

kable(
  head(fight_records_and_sstrikes, 10),
  caption = "Top 10 Fighters in Total Wins(Ascending Order of Losses)")
```

Looking at this table we can see the top 10 fighters with the best win_percentage among fighters with more than 15 total_fights. We can see that Jon Jones has remained in this list as we've continued to make tables. This along with his avg_n_strikes compared to the rest of the list above might suggest that a higher total_significant_strikes or avg_n_sstrikes does not imply a higher win_percentage and this shows as Max Holloway is not in the list above. An outlier in this list to also consider is Islam Makhachev and Ryan Bader who have the lowest total_significant_strikes.
Islam Makhachev is known to predominantly wrestle, going for takedowns and finishing matches with submissions, leading to his low amount of striking. Here is a good point to shift into look at submission stats.

## Takedowns

::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

```{.r .cell-code}
ufc_takedowns <- ufc_agg %>%
  group_by(fighter) %>%
  summarize(
    total_fights = n(),
    total_takedowns = sum(takedown_landed, na.rm = TRUE),
    tot_takedown_attempts = sum(takedown_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    wins = sum(winner == "W", na.rm = TRUE),
    losses = sum(winner == "L", na.rm = TRUE),
    total_ko = sum(result == "KO/TKO" & winner == "W", na.rm = TRUE),
    total_submissions = sum(result == "Submission" & winner == "W", na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  filter(total_fights >= 15) %>%
  mutate(
    takedown_eff = round(total_takedowns / tot_takedown_attempts, 2),
    avg_takedowns = round(total_takedowns / total_fights, 2)
  ) %>%
  arrange(-wins, -total_takedowns)

# Display the first few rows
kable(head(ufc_takedowns, 10), caption = "Top 10 Fighters by Takedowns, KOs, and Submissions")
```
